result:
All done — every test passes (10/10), and the refactored `rotate.sh`/`verify.sh` accept the exact same flags (`--dest`, `--dest=`, `--name`, `--keep=`, `-q/--quiet`, `-n/--dry-run`, `-h/--help`, `--`) with identical exit codes.

What changed:
- **rotate.sh** — `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"` on an oldest-first list, which kept the oldest keep−1 archives and deleted the newest (so with exactly N archives, the newest was removed). It now deletes the oldest `total − keep` entries via `head -n` (guarded for the `total == keep` case, which BSD `head` rejects at 0).
- **verify.sh** — the sidecar file name was extracted with `awk '{print $2}'`, truncating at the first space, so names with spaces looked "archive missing". It now splits the shasum line on the whitespace after the digest, keeping spaces in the name; the digest comparison is quoted too.
- **lib/common.sh** (new) — the shared option-parsing block, `--keep` validation, and `resolve_dir`, sourced by rotate.sh and verify.sh (`source .../lib/common.sh "$@"`); backup.sh, restore.sh and report.sh untouched.
- **tests/run_tests.sh** — added a rotate group (exactly N archives with `--keep N` → nothing deleted, all 3 remain) and a verify group (real archive named `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` → `ok`, rc=0).

Files changed: rotate.sh, verify.sh, tests/run_tests.sh, and new lib/common.sh.
